title: Identification, Synthesis, and In Vitro Activities of Antimicrobial Peptide from African Catfish against the Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL)-Producing Escherichia coli
Identification, Synthesis, and In Vitro Activities of Antimicrobial Peptide from African Catfish against the Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL)-Producing Escherichia coli

comments_text: Discovery: Eight peptides were identified via isolation and characterization by MS. This peptide (97.4% pure) was confirmed to be antimicrobial. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (46.67%) to Rattusin N-terminal fragment 1-8.L: 20%; A=N=R: 13%. Activity: Active against E. coli ATCC 35218 ESBL (MIC 91.3 ug/ml). Activity also confirmed by zone inhibition assay (22 mm). Warning: other bacteria not tested. In vitro toxicity: rabbit RBC, HC50>100 ug/ml, not hemo.lytic. Structure: predicted using both I-TASSER and PEP-FOLD. Provided by and deposited by Hedmon Okella. Reg 5/2025; updated 5/2025
